children: Geopolitical alignment between Canada and Europe won't automatically change business economics, Cornell University visiting professor Vidya Mani says. The significance of Canada's push to become the European Union's first associate member will depend on implementation, Mani says. After all, Canadian and American companies have for decades built deeply integrated supply chains, which can be tough to redirect. The professor says it waits to be seen if a deal between Canada and the EU builds Canadian processing capacity alongside raw material exports, and whether infrastructure funding, partnerships and binding European purchase commitments convert diplomatic ambition into commercially viable investment.
